beats.t: Before they reached the island, the lotus-leaf boat caught in a clump of reeds. Yeongnyangi pressed a paw against the current. Amid the clinking mirror shards came a faint grinding of teeth. Yeoni pricked up their pig ears. It almost sounded like someone holding back tears.
Over there. Something's under the reeds. Like a black ball of fluff. Wait, it has eyes. I'm not just looking at a doll that fell in the water, am I?

A little cloak edged with gold thread was tangled in the reeds. A striped tail wriggled beneath it. A black tiger. Even wet, its red eyes were bright, and the marking on its forehead glowed red as a wound. A black loop finer than thread encircled its right forepaw.
If you're done staring, leave. I can recognize pity even reflected in water. And I'm not a ball of fluff. Take that back first.
You can talk, too. Then you can ask to be rescued. Just say you need help. Your paw's shaking like that—pretending you're fine only makes it hurt more.
Wait. Don't touch it. That is no animal trap. It is a ring seeking an owner. Touch it and it will ask your name. Answer, and you will be bound to that one.

Yeoni stopped with a hoof outstretched. They were not even certain of the body or name they would return to. But the ring tightened every time the tiger drew breath. Turning the boat away and leaving that tiny paw behind felt more frightening.
So I just don't give it my name? Then let's not talk it open. I'll use this. Yeongnyangi, just keep the boat steady. I'm scared too, so save the complicated explanations for later.

Yeoni picked up a dry leaf stalk from the boat's edge in their mouth. Black water spurted as they pushed it between the ring and the fur. The tiger reflexively lashed at Yeoni's nose, then stopped. The stalk snapped. The ring was still tight.
Stop. You can't even control your own body. Who do you think you'll save with paws like that? If you get hurt, will you charge me for it?
If it hurts, say it hurts. Stop putting a price tag on everything. I didn't negotiate this long the day I dropped my rice triangle. You're the one who needs help right now.

Gold gathered at the tips of Yeongnyangi's claws. A direct cut at that angle would injure the tiger's paw too. Yeongnyangi withdrew the blade-like light and tilted the leaf. The current changed direction. For one brief instant, the taut ring loosened.
Now. Push, don't pull. Don't try to force the ring past it. Make room for the paw to slip free.

Yeoni pressed their forehead against the tiger's shoulder. They rolled together onto the wet leaf. The ring stayed behind in the river and contracted, clutching at empty air. It bit three times at the place the paw had been, then burst into black foam.
Why did you push with your own body? You could have been hurt. You could have ordered that cat in the hat to do it. That's what the power to give orders is for.
Why would asking a friend be an order? Besides, I only just found this out myself. A pig's forehead is surprisingly useful. Ow. My nose, on the other hand, is just uselessly sore.

The tiger looked at the scratch on Yeoni's nose. Red eyes narrowed while it tugged at the hem of its cloak. A child who did not retreat even after getting hurt. The tiger studied Yeoni's expression for a long time, measuring how close a single pained face might draw this child.
Tell me what you want. Directions, an object, anything. Debts grow if you leave them. Settling this now would be easier for us both.
As long as you're okay, that's enough. If I had to ask for one thing... your name? You seem like you'd get angry if I kept calling you Tiger.
A name isn't something you give away lightly. Once you hold it, you can call me wherever I am. A life spent answering anyone who calls isn't much of a life.
Then you don't have to give it. I'll just call you Tiger. I don't need to know someone's name to help them.

The tiger's tail went still. A droplet fell from the gold clasp and rolled across the leaf. Yeongnyangi saw it crawl toward the tiger instead of returning to the river. Without a word, a paw came down between Yeoni and the tiger.
We travel together as far as the landing. After that, we go our separate ways. I won't ask who sent you. Don't ask this child's name either.
Are all cats in hats this unfriendly? You free one little paw and start putting up fences. Afraid I'll bite your friend?
I thought he was a big cat at first, too. He really hates that, though. Do you hate being called a little tiger?
Leave out 'little.' Ranking people by size is a thoroughly outdated habit. Count the cloak, and I'm not even that small.

Yeoni laughed. Instead of joining in, the tiger lowered its ears. Yeoni's gaze held little wariness toward this small, soaked animal. When the tiger hid its reddened ears under the cloak, Yeoni only softened their voice further. The tiger remembered that difference.
Sit over there where it's dry. Your cloak must be heavy with all that water. All that gold trim looks cool, but washing it must be a nightmare.

The tiger held out the cloak's hem. A black thread hidden inside the gold edging slipped among the fabric's red fibers. When Yeongnyangi turned, it stopped. The tiger licked its wet paw as though nothing had happened.
Hold this against your nose. Drying the water should make it sting less. I'm not giving you the cloak, so don't start thinking it's yours.
Got it. Borrowing. Thank you. You sound scary, but your hands are kinder than I expected. Or paws, I guess.

The island's bell rang. The tiger pricked its ears at the first note and leaped from the boat before the second. Its injured paw never touched the water. The black surface briefly hardened, becoming a narrow path wherever it stepped.
Do not follow those tracks. A creature that makes roads across water did not get trapped because it lost its way.
You mean it got caught on purpose? Then was the pain an act too? I thought that face was real. I know a little about the face people make when they're holding pain in.
Real pain and a hidden motive can exist together. You must see both. That does not make your choice to help wrong.

Yeoni pulled a red strand from the cloak off their nose and laid it on a hoof. Somehow, they could not throw it away. Beyond the island mist, the black tiger looked back. Its smile was gone. Only two red points remained above the water.
So you stop when you see someone hurt. Wherever you go, now I know who to put in your path. Next time, come where that cat isn't.

The pain of the ring crossing the boundary had been real. But what the tiger had stolen was not a route. It was Yeoni's reaction. The broken end of a black thread from the cloak sank into the river. Beneath it, someone's name was silently erased.
